display_title: Measurement-System Validation for a Game-Playing AI: Bayesian Opponent Modelling and Sequential Testing (Kaggle PTCG AI Battle Challenge)
one_liner: Two-person Kaggle entry in which the most important findings were three faults in our own test harness. Finding them is what separated real improvements from measurement artifacts.
problem: Build a program that plays a hidden-information card game against thousands of other agents. Five shared submissions a day and a ladder whose single reading carries about ±125 rating points of noise make every improvement hard to verify.
approach: Rule-based policy with 1-ply forward search. A hypergeometric Bayesian posterior over opponent decklists, built from 146k mined decks. Sequential probability ratio tests for agent changes. Instrument validation (symmetry, determinism, distribution checks against real replays). A ladder-episode store for rating-band-conditioned matchup and loss analysis.
decision_relevance: The same failure modes appear in combat-model and wargame analysis: a simulator whose scoring rule penalises only one side, 'paired' random seeds that are not paired, self-play benchmarks where shared errors cancel, and decisions read off a single stochastic run. The project quantifies each one and shows how it was caught.

headline_results.claim: An identical agent resubmitted scores 93-150 rating points apart (noise floor ~125). A single leaderboard submission cannot resolve differences below ~150.
headline_results.evidence: GLIDEPATH.md s2d; README 'A single submission's score is worth ±150 points' (4 identical-submission pairs)

headline_results.claim: Opponent-decklist posterior graded on 300 replays with both real decklists known: 99.7% prior coverage, top-1 accuracy 0.63 (turn 1), 0.84 (turn 3), 0.94 (turn 10), well calibrated. 80% of misidentifications are near-identical sister lists.
headline_results.evidence: scripts/validate_posterior.py, scripts/misid_cost.py; README 'Lookahead'; GLIDEPATH s3 (output file not tracked)

headline_results.claim: Found three test-harness faults that invalidated recorded evidence: legal empty moves scored as forfeits for opponents only (24.9% vs 0%), an engine that was never actually seeded, and 300-game cells that flipped sign at 600 games. Example correction: Archaludon matchup 0.887 -> 0.32.
headline_results.evidence: GLIDEPATH.md s2a-2c; FINDINGS_v3_to_v9.md s1; ptcg/arena.py fix; scripts/harness_selftest.py

headline_results.claim: Local self-play harness reports 0.892 against the encounter-weighted field where the ladder shows 0.519. The bias grows with how much piloting skill the opponent's deck needs (+0.25 to +0.78).

Grader-environment probes found silent production failures: exec()-loaded main.py has no __file__, the last callable becomes the entry point, and a lazy import disabled search on every submission (0 -> 273 search calls after fix).

An apparent 0.532 -> 0.294 drop against the plurality archetype (z=1.68) was killed as a rating-band confound without spending a submission. The win rate is monotone in opponent rating (0.750/0.533/0.368/0.000).
Metagame mined from 146,376 decks over 16 days: ~120-204 distinct decklists, with the top 40 lists covering 94.4% of play.

limitations: Every local matchup win rate is an upper bound: our own agent pilots both sides (symmetric-pilot bias up to +0.78).
The pre-2026-08-09 SPRT decision ledger ran on 82-511 unseeded games with forfeit inflation and is provisional.
Engine seed pinning works only on macOS/Linux (LD_PRELOAD/DYLD). Pinned runs cannot be reproduced on Windows.
The battle engine is competition-use-only and not redistributable, so game-outcome results cannot be reproduced from the public repo.
Ladder autopsy rows are small-n (5-32 games per archetype-band cell), and the 900+ band has 20 games.
Two-person team: agent internals, the seed fix and the engine-arithmetic fixes are the teammate's (Austin S) work.
